correctness.rationale: For every connected finite unweighted d-regular bipartite graph, its checkerboard sign vector is an eigenvector Ls=2ds. All odd reaction powers preserve the invariant line. The exact scalar reaction flow R_t(x)=e^t x/(1+(e^{2pt}-1)|x|^{2p})^(1/(2p)), and diffusion scales by exp(-lambda t). Composition of either Strang order is F(x)=a x/(1+b|x|^{2p})^(1/(2p)), a=e^{(1-lambda)tau}>1,b>0; the reciprocal power recurrence is affine contraction, proving exactly three fixed points, sign-conditional attraction and derivative exp(-2p(1-lambda)tau). Algebra gives claimed hyperbolic x_D and x_R powers; sinh(z)/z strict increase yields crossover at lambda=1/2 and order relation. Addition identity gives x_R^{2p}/x_D^{2p}=cosh(p tau/2)/cosh(p(1-2lambda)tau/2); logarithmic growth rate is one half min(lambda,1-lambda), independent of p. Independent 27 cases validated amplitudes and ratio; analytic proof covers all p, graph sizes and positive steps. Transverse stability deliberately not claimed.
residual_risks: Results only on invariant checkerboard line; transverse stability in full graph state space not proved.
Requires 0<lambda<1, odd powers, regular unweighted connected bipartite graph, exact flows; not arbitrary PDE discretization.
Historical broad scalar splitting theory could imply these elementary exact-flow identities as a specialized corollary despite no identified explicit statement.

value.rationale: A sharp, unconditional-in-step, graph-wide classification of equilibrium bias for a natural invariant nonlinear reaction–diffusion mode is useful for numerical splitting choices: switching symmetric order can invert bias, and reaction-outside preserves the continuous equilibrium exactly at a nontrivial threshold. Full fixed point dynamics and power-independent exponential separation add structural content beyond the general fact that splitting perturbs equilibria.
